newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Citibank cashes in on Asia's credit-hungry market.
newsitem.headline: Citibank cashes in on Asia's credit-hungry market.

text.p: Citibank is reaping rich dividends in the Philippines and other Asian markets where its credit card business is growing at robust rates, a senior bank official said Monday.

Business in the Philippines was booming with growth rates seen at 30 percent to 40 percent annually, Harpal Dugal, vice president and business manager for Citibank Philippines credit card divison, said in an interview.
The growth comes on top of a threefold increase in the size of the business in the past three years.

Total annual spending in the Philippines through credit cards had risen to between 45 billion pesos ($1.72 billion) and 50 billion pesos ($1.9 billion) annually from 16 billion to 18 billion pesos ($61.1 million to 68.7 million) in 1993, he said.

Citibank Philippines, a unit of Citicorp, dominates the business with its cards accounting for 14 billion to 15 billion pesos ($53.4 million to 57.3 million) out of a total spending of 45 billion to 50 billion pesos ($1.7 billion to 1.9 billion).

Dugal declined to give profit figures for Citibank's credit card business in the Philippines but said it accounted for about 65 percent to 70 percent of profits in its consumer banking division and about 30 percent to 35 percent of total profits.
